name: national-id-field
title: National ID field
description: A personal identity number per country, such as a Dutch BSN or a US SSN, formatted as printed and checked with its own checksum, masked by default.
docs: value and onValueChange speak the number without separators and { valid, country }: valid is true when the number is complete and passes its country's checks. country and onCountryChange choose the country by ISO code (defaultCountry when you do not control it); the menu comes with Belgium, Canada, Germany, Spain, France, the United Kingdom, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden and the United States, each with its own arithmetic (the Dutch eleven test, the Luhn digit, the Spanish check letter, the Italian check character, the areas of a Social Security number that are never issued), and countries adds a country or replaces one with a rule of your own { name, label, describe, example, maxLength, keyboard, clean, format, check, messages }. The number is written as it is printed (111 222 333, 123-45-6789, AB 12 34 56 C) and only the characters of that country are accepted. A wrong number is explained in words (A BSN has nine digits and passes the eleven test) once the field has been left, or at once when the number is as long as it gets, and the words never repeat the number, so nothing is read out, logged or kept. With masked (the default) the number is hidden behind dots as soon as the field is left and a button, named Show number, shows it again; masked={false} keeps it in view. autoComplete is off and password managers are told to ignore the field. name adds a hidden input with the number and <name>-country with the country; id lands on the number input. The checks are arithmetic only, so they catch a typo, not a number that was never issued. checkNationalId, isNationalId, formatNationalId and the table itself are plain functions in national-id-field/ids.
